Center Ride Out

April 23–25, 2027

Friday, April 23 through Sunday, April 25, 2027. Check-in is Thursday, April 22, 3:00 to 7:00 pm, at the Los Angeles LGBT Center. The first ride was April 24–26, 2026.

Sign up for Center Ride Out Official site (centerrideout.lalgbtcenter.org)

Registration is $95 for 3-day riders and $195 for 1-day riders. The fundraising minimum is $2,500 for 3-day riders (the ride’s page gives April 2, 2027) and $250 for 1-day riders (by April 23). A Community Fund can cover a minimum or a registration; its 2027 applications open in February.

04.23 Los Angeles

What is the Center Ride Out?

Center Ride Out is a three-day, 200-plus-mile supported ride that raises money for the Los Angeles LGBT Center. In 2027 it runs April 23–25: Los Angeles to Ojai, a day at camp by a lake, then back along the coast to a finish near Santa Monica. Registration is $95 and the fundraising minimum is $2,500 for 3-day riders. The first ride, in 2026, went from Los Angeles to San Diego and raised $830,511.

How Center Ride Out started

AIDS/LifeCycle ran from San Francisco to Los Angeles for seven days every June and raised more than $300 million for HIV and AIDS services from 1994 on. Its last ride was in 2025. The Los Angeles LGBT Center announced Center Ride Out in November 2025 as the ride that carries that legacy in Southern California.

The first Center Ride Out was April 24–26, 2026, from Los Angeles to San Diego. The Center says it raised $830,511. For 2027 the route changes: north to Ojai, a camp there, and back down the coast.

What to expect on the day

Check-in is the afternoon before, at the Center: wristbands, bike drop-off, and you meet the volunteers. Friday rolls at 6:30 am. Routes close between 3:00 and 6:00 pm, depending on the day’s length.

The ride is fully supported. Rest stops come every 15 to 20 miles, lunch is on the route, and there are support vehicles, bike mechanics, a marked course and medical staff on the road and in camp. You don’t have to ride every mile. A support vehicle will take you to the next stop, to lunch or to camp.

Camp is in Ojai, by a lake. The Center calls it Queer Summer Camp: swimming, canoeing, a DJ, s’mores, massages and a stage program at night. Saturday you can stay there or ride an out-and-back. Sunday rolls by 7:00 am and ends at a finish line festival by the ocean with food and music.

The town guide

Ride, sleep, eat, fix the bike.

Los Angeles is a cycling city in zones: a 22-mile car-free beach path from Will Rogers State Beach to Torrance, canyon climbs in the Santa Monica Mountains above Malibu, Griffith Park’s car-free roads and the LA River path on the east side, and Glendora Mountain Road in the San Gabriels. The zones sit 20 to 40 miles apart, so most visitors rent a car. Alaska, Southwest, Delta and American all check a packed bike as a standard bag (Sept 2026), one West Hollywood shop builds a shipped one, and two Santa Monica shops rent a road bike. Bring yours for three days or more.

Fly into LAX (about 12 miles from downtown, closest to the Westside) or Burbank (about 12 miles, closer to Griffith Park, the Valley and the Pasadena side; a smaller airport that is faster to get out of). Long Beach is the South Bay airport, Ontario the one for Glendora Mountain Road. You will want a car: the zones are 20 to 40 miles apart, and rental offices at LAX are off airport by free shuttle. Ride apps pick up at the LAX-it lot next to Terminal 1; book an XL for the bike case. The Bring-your-bike page has the airline rules, the shipping option and Metro’s bike rules.

Center Ride Out FAQ

When is Center Ride Out in 2027?

April 23–25, 2027, a Friday through a Sunday. Check-in is Thursday, April 22, from 3:00 to 7:00 pm at the Los Angeles LGBT Center.

What is the Center Ride Out route?

In 2027 it goes from Los Angeles north through canyon and mountain roads to Ojai on Day 1, 80-plus miles. Day 2 is a day in camp or an out-and-back ride. Day 3 goes from Ojai back to the coast and finishes near Santa Monica, 80-plus miles. The Center says route links come closer to the ride and the routes may change. The 2026 ride went from Los Angeles to San Diego.

What is the fundraising minimum?

$2,500 for 3-day riders and $250 for 1-day riders. Registration is $95 for three days and $195 for one.

Where do riders sleep?

In camp in Ojai, by a lake, on Friday and Saturday nights. The Center has not published the camp’s location. People who aren’t riding or volunteering can buy a $50 Basecamp pass.

Can I ride just one day?

Yes. 1-day riders ride Day 2, Saturday, April 24.

Where does the money go?

To the Los Angeles LGBT Center’s general fund. The Center says about 89 cents of every dollar raised goes to its programs and services.
